ERPNext · Assets · Asset Workspace

Asset Module Guide

How to record the laptops, monitors, phones and software subscriptions the company gives its people, who holds each one, and what each employee and department costs.

MACBOOK AIR M1 - 001
Where/app/asset-workspace, or Asset Workspace in the Assets sidebar
Built onERPNext's standard Asset, Asset Category, Item and Asset Movement records
TracksIT Hardware and Subscriptions, each mapped to an employee

What the module does

Every asset the company owns is a record in ERPNext's normal Asset list. The Asset Module adds three things on top of it:

  • A clear hierarchy for every asset: Category, Sub-Category, Item and the asset itself.
  • Employee mapping. Each asset shows the employee who holds it (its Custodian) and keeps a full history of who held it before.
  • The Asset Workspace, one screen to see everything, hand out and take back assets in a couple of clicks, and run cost reports.
One list, one process

There is no second asset register. An asset created on the standard Asset form appears in the Asset Workspace straight away. An assignment made in the Asset Workspace is a standard Asset Movement you can also see in ERPNext.

How assets are organised

Every asset sits in a four-level hierarchy. Here is the path for one laptop:

CategoryIT HardwareAsset Category
Sub-CategoryLaptopItem Group
ItemMacbook Air M1Item (Fixed Asset)
AssetMACBOOK AIR M1 - 001Asset

The line in blue under each level is the ERPNext record that stores it.

The two categories in use today

CategoryTypeSub-categoriesExample items
IT HardwareHardwareLaptop, Monitor, Mobile Phone, AccessoriesMacbook Air M1, Dell Latitude 5440, Dell P2422H 24 inch, iPhone 13, Logitech MX Keys
SubscriptionsSubscriptionProductivity Suite, Design Software, Developer Tools, CommunicationMicrosoft 365 Business Standard, Figma Professional, GitHub Copilot Business, Slack Pro

Hardware assets carry a serial number and a warranty date. Subscription assets carry a licence ID, a billing cycle (monthly or yearly) and a renewal date. Each subscription asset is one seat. Four Microsoft 365 licences are four assets.

How assets are named

When you create an asset, ERPNext names it after its item and adds the next number for that item. The first Macbook Air M1 is MACBOOK AIR M1 - 001, the fifth is Macbook Air M1 - 005. Each item keeps its own count, and the name is also copied into the asset's Asset Name, so the Asset list shows it.

Opening it and who can use it

Three ways in:

  • Go to /app/asset-workspace on your ERPNext site.
  • Open the Assets module and click Asset Workspace in the sidebar, just under Asset.
  • Press Ctrl + G (the ERPNext search bar), type Asset Workspace and press Enter.

The Asset Workspace opens full screen. The grid icon at the top right takes you back to ERPNext, and the sun/moon icon switches between dark and light mode.

Who can do what

Access follows ERPNext's standard roles. Ask your System Manager to give you the role you need.

To do thisYou need one of these roles
Open the Asset Workspace and see reportsAccounts User, Accounts Manager, Quality Manager, Stock Manager, System Manager
Create and submit assetsAccounts User, Quality Manager
Assign and return assets (submit an Asset Movement)Accounts Manager, Stock Manager, System Manager
Add a categoryAccounts User, Accounts Manager, Quality Manager
Add a sub-category or an itemItem Manager

The Asset Workspace, tab by tab

The tabs at the top are Dashboard, Assign & Return, Employees, Assets and Reports. The gear icon opens the Catalogue.

Dashboard

Totals for all assets: assigned, available and still in Draft, what subscriptions cost per month, and the value of the hardware. Below that is one card per category, with how many assets in each sub-category are assigned. Then come warranties and renewals that are overdue or due within 45 days, and the latest assignments and returns. Click a category card to open its assets.

Assign & Return

The everyday screen. On the left are the assets ready to hand out; on the right, the assets employees have now. Search, or filter by category and sub-category, to find an asset quickly. How to use it is under Assigning and returning.

Employees

Every active employee, with how many hardware assets and subscriptions they hold. Use the chips to show only people holding assets, or only people without any. Click an employee to see what they hold now, the full history of what they held before, and buttons to assign or return.

Assets

Every asset with its item, category, status, holder, warranty or renewal date and cost. Filter by category, sub-category and status, or search by asset name, serial number or employee. Click an asset to see its details, who holds it and every past assignment.

Reports

Eleven reports, from the cost of each employee to unused subscription seats. See Reports.

Catalogue (gear icon)

The whole hierarchy on one page: each category, its sub-categories, their items, and how many assets of each item exist, are assigned and are free. Its buttons open the standard ERPNext forms. See Categories, sub-categories, items.

Adding assets

Assets are created on ERPNext's standard Asset form. To open it, use any of these:

  • + Add Asset in the Asset list.
  • New asset on the Asset Workspace dashboard or the Assets tab.
  • + Asset next to an item in the Catalogue. The form opens with that item already filled in.

Steps

  1. Item Code. Pick the item, for example Macbook Air M1. Asset Category and Sub-Category fill themselves in.
  2. Asset Type. Choose Existing Asset for something you already own that was not bought through an ERPNext Purchase Receipt or Invoice. If it was bought through ERPNext, link that Purchase Receipt or Invoice instead, as you normally would.
  3. Company and Location, for example Head Office.
  4. Purchase Date, Available-for-use Date and Net Purchase Amount. For a subscription, enter the price per billing cycle, for example ₹770 for a monthly Microsoft 365 seat.
  5. Serial No / Licence ID, Warranty / Renewal Date and, for subscriptions, Billing Cycle (Monthly or Yearly).
  6. Save. The asset gets its name, for example Macbook Air M1 - 005.
  7. Submit. An asset must be submitted before it can be assigned to anyone. Until then it shows as Draft.
Depreciation

The module does not post accounting entries of its own. Tick Calculate Depreciation on an asset, or set it up on its Asset Category, only if your accounts team wants ERPNext to depreciate it. The Subscriptions category is set so it never depreciates.

Assigning and returning

Giving an asset to an employee, or taking it back, creates a standard ERPNext Asset Movement:

  • Assign creates an Issue movement and sets the asset's Custodian to that employee.
  • Return creates a Receipt movement back to the asset's location and clears the Custodian.

Both are submitted for you. The message that confirms the action names the movement, for example ACC-ASM-2026-00084.

Assign one or more assets

  1. Open Assign & Return.
  2. In Available, tick the assets to hand out. To give one asset only, you can instead click Assign on its row.
  3. Click Assign selected.
  4. Search for the Employee by name or ID, check the Assigned on date, and click Assign.

You can also assign from an employee's page (Assign asset), from the Employees list (Assign on a row), or from an asset's page (Assign).

Return assets

  1. In With employees, tick the assets coming back, or click Return on one row.
  2. Click Return selected, check the Returned on date, and click Return.

When someone hands back everything, open their page under Employees and use Return all.

Moving an asset from one employee to another

Return it first, then assign it to the new person. The Asset Workspace will not assign an asset that someone already holds; it asks you to return it first.

Doing the same in ERPNext directly

Anyone used to ERPNext can make the movement by hand. Open Asset Movement and click + Add, then:

  • To assign: set Purpose to Issue, and add a row with the Asset and the To Employee.
  • To return: set Purpose to Receipt, and add a row with the Asset, the From Employee and the Target Location.

Submit it. The Asset Workspace shows the change immediately, because it reads the same records.

Dates must move forward

A movement cannot be dated before the asset's previous movement. If you backdate an assignment to before the asset's last return, ERPNext refuses with “Transaction date can't be earlier than previous movement date”. Pick a later date.

Categories, sub-categories, items

Open the Catalogue with the gear icon. Each button opens the standard ERPNext form with the right values already filled in. Save the form there, then come back to the Asset Workspace.

ButtonOpensFilled in for you
+ Asset CategoryNew Asset CategoryNothing. Set the name, the Category Type (Hardware or Subscription) and one Accounts row with your company's fixed asset account.
+ Sub-categoryNew Item GroupParent Item Group = the category. The category's own group is created automatically the first time.
+ ItemNew ItemItem Group = the sub-category, Asset Category, Is Fixed Asset ticked, Maintain Stock off
+ AssetNew AssetItem Code
Pencil iconThat recordUse it to edit a category, sub-category or item. Keep a category's name and its Item Group's name the same.
Where a sub-category belongs

A sub-category is an Item Group whose parent is a group with the same name as the category. For example, Laptop sits under the Item Group IT Hardware. Keep to this when creating Item Groups by hand, or the sub-category will not appear under its category.

Subscriptions

  • One asset per seat or licence. Eight Slack seats are eight assets, so each seat can be given to one person.
  • Net Purchase Amount is the price for one billing cycle. Set Billing Cycle to Monthly or Yearly. The reports convert it: a yearly ₹13,200 Zoom seat counts as ₹1,100 a month.
  • Warranty / Renewal Date is the next renewal. When a subscription renews, open the asset and move this date on. The field can be changed on a submitted asset.
  • Unassigned seats still cost money. The Subscription seats report shows what unused seats cost per month.

Leavers, repairs, disposal

When an employee leaves

  1. Run Reports › Leavers holding assets. It lists every asset still held by an employee whose status is no longer Active.
  2. Collect the items, open the employee's page and click Return all.
  3. Free up or cancel their subscription seats so the company stops paying for them.

Repairs

Use ERPNext's standard Asset Repair or Asset Maintenance. While ERPNext marks an asset In Maintenance or Out of Order, the Asset Workspace shows it as Under Repair and it cannot be assigned.

Selling or scrapping

Use ERPNext's standard Scrap Asset or Sell Asset actions on the Asset form. The asset then shows as Disposed and drops out of the cost reports. Return it from the employee first.

The Asset Workspace works out each asset's status from its ERPNext record:

StatusMeansComes from
AvailableReady to hand outSubmitted, with no Custodian
AssignedAn employee has itSubmitted, with a Custodian (set by an Issue movement)
DraftSaved but not submitted; cannot be assigned yetAsset not submitted
Under RepairOut of use for repairERPNext status In Maintenance or Out of Order
DisposedNo longer owned or in useERPNext status Scrapped, Sold or Capitalized

Reports

Open the Reports tab and pick a report from the chips. Every report has:

  • summary figures at the top and a bar chart
  • a table with totals at the bottom; click any column heading to sort, and click a row to open that employee or asset
  • a search box and filters (category, department, a date range or time window where relevant)
  • an Excel button that downloads exactly the rows you see, with your search and sort applied
ReportAnswersFilters

How costs are calculated

Hardware valueNet Purchase Amount of the asset
Subscription per monthMonthly: the cost · Yearly: cost ÷ 12
Monthly costsubscriptions per month + hardware value ÷ 36
Annual costmonthly cost × 12
Subscription spend to dateper-month cost × days held ÷ 30.44, summed over every period the employee held the seat
Utilisationassigned units ÷ all units
Renewal cost in windowevery renewal inside the window; a monthly seat renews 12 times in 12 months

The 36 months spread a laptop's price over three years of use, so it can sit beside monthly subscription costs. The hardware value itself is shown separately as well.

Questions and errors

An asset I just created is not in the Available list

It is probably still a Draft. Open it and click Submit. The Assign & Return screen shows a banner when draft assets exist, with a link to them. Assets that are Under Repair or Disposed are not listed either.

“… is already with [name]. Return it first.”

Someone holds that asset. Return it from them, then assign it to the new person.

“Transaction date can't be earlier than previous movement date”

You picked a date before the asset's last movement. Use a date on or after its last assignment or return. The asset's page lists those dates under Assignment history.

“… is not submitted yet. Submit the Asset first.”

Only submitted assets can be assigned. Open the asset and submit it.

“You do not have permission for this.”

Your role does not allow that action. Assigning and returning needs Accounts Manager, Stock Manager or System Manager. See Who can do what.

I want an asset named the old way (ACC-ASS-2026-00001)

On the Asset form, change Naming Series to ACC-ASS-.YYYY.- before saving. The item-based name is only the default.

Where is the full history of an asset stored?

In its submitted Asset Movements. Open the Asset Movement list filtered by the asset, or the ERPNext Asset Activity report. The asset's page in the Asset Workspace shows the same history as a list of who held it and when.

Can I undo an assignment made by mistake?

Return the asset with today's date. Alternatively, an Accounts Manager can cancel the Asset Movement in ERPNext; the Custodian then goes back to what it was before.

The Asset Workspace says “Page not found”

The app is not installed on this site yet, or the server has not been restarted since. Ask your administrator to follow the steps in For administrators.

Glossary

Asset
One physical item or one subscription seat, for example Macbook Air M1 - 001.
Asset Category
The top level: IT Hardware or Subscriptions. It also holds the accounting settings.
Item Group
ERPNext's grouping of items; here it holds the sub-categories (Laptop, Monitor, …).
Item
The model or product, such as Macbook Air M1, marked as a Fixed Asset item.
Custodian
The employee who holds an asset right now.
Asset Movement
The ERPNext record of an asset changing hands or place. Issue gives it to an employee; Receipt brings it back.
Existing Asset
An asset type for things owned before they were entered in ERPNext, with no purchase document.
Submit
Confirm a record in ERPNext. Submitted assets and movements are final; changing one means cancelling it.
Billing Cycle
How often a subscription is paid: Monthly or Yearly.
Utilisation
The share of units that are assigned to someone.

For administrators

The module is its own Frappe app, asset_management. It needs only ERPNext v16 and does not depend on any other custom app. Installing it on a site:

bench get-app <repo-url> asset_management
bench --site <site> backup
bench --site <site> install-app asset_management
bench build --app asset_management
bench restart

To update it later, pull the new code, then run bench --site <site> migrate and bench restart. Always restart after installing or updating, because the web server and background workers only load new app code when they start.

Every migrate re-applies the module's setup:

  • the custom fields on Asset and Asset Category
  • the default naming series .{item_name}. - .###
  • the Custodian column in the Asset list
  • the Asset Workspace link in the Assets sidebar

It does not change existing assets.

Sample data

For a demo or staging site only. It creates 2 categories, 8 sub-categories, 16 items, 44 submitted assets, 8 sample employees and their Asset Movements under the site's default company. It is safe to run twice.

bench --site <site> execute asset_management.asset_management.sample_data.load
Not for production

The sample employees and assets look real. Run the loader only where test data is expected.
